record.category: model and dataset registry with a CDN (anonymous read)

free_tier.stated: Anonymous download of any public model or dataset file, no token. The published per-5-minute windows are API 500, Resolvers 3,000, Pages 100 for an anonymous caller, and 1,000 / 5,000 / 200 for a free account; 'All quotas are calculated over 5-minute fixed windows.'
free_tier.notes: Bytes are not metered at all; only request counts are.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable per file; a repository may hold very large files. The file measured here is 548,118,077 bytes (openai-community/gpt2 pytorch_model.bin).

retention.stated: until the repository owner deletes or revises the revision; anonymous readers can pin a commit hash to keep a fixed object

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. /resolve/ redirects to a CDN host (us.aws.cdn.hf.co through the xet bridge) with a short-lived signed URL; the signature is issued to the anonymous caller and no token is involved.

record.interface_detail: GET https://huggingface.co/<repo>/resolve/<rev>/<path> for a file; the API at /api/models and /api/datasets; the dataset viewer at datasets-server.huggingface.co (rows, parquet, size); hf CLI and git for repo-level sync.
record.tooling: hf CLI, huggingface_hub python, git-lfs, plain curl on /resolve/. rclone reads it through the HTTP remote. The dataset viewer's /parquet endpoint hands back per-file parquet URLs that a client can fetch directly.
record.chaining: The fastest measured pipe among debrid providers and the only one whose content is current ML data rather than a fixed corpus: pull a dataset's parquet parts for training, and mirror the same files to storage with rclone. Common Crawl now mirrors selected crawls into an HF Storage Bucket, so both paths can share one client.

limits.value: anonymous: 500 API, 3,000 Resolvers, 100 Pages per 5-minute window; free account doubles all three
measured here: one connection sustained 34.8-36.6 MiB/s on a 256 MiB range and 39.98 MiB/s on a 548 MB file, while eight parallel range requests totalled only 17.1-21.3 MiB/s

record.limits_note: Whether the 8-connection drop is Hugging Face's CDN, the ISP shaping parallel flows, or the line itself was not established: the Cloudflare speed test endpoint refused this network with 403, so there is no independent line-ceiling measurement.
record.binding_note: Request counts never bind at this scale - 3,000 resolver calls per 5 minutes is 864,000 a day, far more files than a TiB holds. What limits a day is the ~36-40 MiB/s ceiling, and adding connections lowers it rather than raising it.

identity_cost.detail: No token: https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 returned 401 for an anonymous client, and the same client downloaded 548,118,077 bytes from /resolve/ successfully. A free account doubles the request windows; it buys no bytes.

record.reliability_note: The /resolve/ URL redirects to a signed CDN URL that expires; a client must follow the redirect per request rather than cache the final URL. Anonymous windows are explicitly 'subject to change over time depending on platform health'.
record.confidence_note: A complete 548 MB file was downloaded and hashed, and three 256 MiB runs at each concurrency were recorded. The extrapolation to bytes/day is arithmetic on those numbers, not a 24-hour run.

evidence.proved: the per-5-minute windows: anonymous 500 API / 3,000 Resolvers / 100 Pages; free account 1,000 / 5,000 / 200
full file: 200, 548,118,077 bytes, sha256 7c5d3f4b8b76583b422fcb9189ad6c89d5d97a094541ce8932dce3ecabde1421, 13,072.6 ms = 39.98 MiB/s over one connection
256 MiB at one connection: 36.593, 34.818, 36.610 MiB/s across three runs
256 MiB over eight connections: 17.058, 21.332, 20.440 MiB/s total, each below its own one-connection baseline - parallelism loses
401 with www-authenticate: Bearer - there was no token in the client that downloaded the 548 MB file
200, 61,691 bytes for 100 rows, anonymous - the dataset viewer is readable without a token

record.notes: About 40 MiB/s over one connection with no account, which is 3.3 TiB/day if the rate held for a day. The eight-connection run is the trap - it is half the speed, so a client that opens eight streams to go faster gets there slower.

free_tier.stated: 'Do you have an awesome Space but need help covering the GPU hardware upgrade costs? We love helping out those with an innovative Space so please feel free to apply for a community GPU grant and see if yours makes the cut! This application can be found in your Space hardware repo settings in the lower left corner under "sleep time settings"'. There is also a lighter path, quoted: 'You can even request a free upgrade if you are building a cool demo for a side project!' The unit is a hardware tier attached to one Space, not a credit balance, and billing is quoted as 'based on hardware usage and is computed by the minute'.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The grant is a route to a dedicated, always-on GPU behind a public URL with no card: a free account gets 2 ZeroGPU Spaces with 5 minutes of GPU a day (the compute record huggingface-spaces-zerogpu), and this grant is what a project applies for when 96 GB and a 5 minute window are not enough. It composes with inference APIs because the Space can sit in front of an external API and hold the connection. Hardware table on the Spaces GPU page (column 'Hourly Price', billed by the minute while a Space is Starting or Running; the page has no on-demand, spot or community label and states no minimum bill): 1x Nvidia L4 24 GB $0.80, 1x Nvidia L40S 48 GB $1.80, Nvidia A100 - large 80 GB $2.50. The Nvidia H100 rows are struck through and marked 'removed December 2025'. No GeForce row.

limits.value: the grant is attached to a single Space rather than to an account: approval is discretionary, it covers the hardware tier of that Space only, and nothing in the record says the hours can be moved to a training job.

record.notes: Distinct from the ZeroGPU record already in earlier readings: ZeroGPU is a quota every free account holds, while a community GPU grant is a discretionary hardware allocation to one Space. The amount is unverified and deliberately so: the docs publish no tier list, no hour count and no approval rate, and the public applications found on Spaces range from a demo to 2,500 GPU hours, so the honest claim is the mechanism. A 'community grant' could cover hardware only, hardware plus storage, or a cash-equivalent credit. The docs describe hardware ('covering the GPU hardware upgrade costs') and a public applicant asked for storage separately, which supports hardware-only.

record.provider: Hugging Face Storage Buckets via S3 gateway (s3.hf.co) — as an annex/DVC backend
record.category: S3-compatible object storage (Hugging Face Storage Buckets through the s3.hf.co gateway)

free_tier.stated: Free user or organisation: public storage 'Best-effort' with no published figure, private storage 100 GB; the storage plans and policies apply to every repository type, buckets included
free_tier.notes: above the first few gigabytes of public storage the page asks for content of value to other users and names abuse mitigations without a figure; PRO, Team and Enterprise plans carry numeric public and private limits

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: the 500 GB per-file hard limit on the storage-limits page is stated in a section marked as not applying to Storage Buckets, and the bucket and S3 gateway pages publish no per-object limit
per_object_cap.notes: Git-backed model, dataset and Space repositories keep the 500 GB per-file hard limit

retention.stated: unverified: the bucket, S3 gateway and storage-limits pages state no expiry or inactivity rule for stored objects; incomplete multipart uploads expire after 7 days
retention.notes: buckets are non-versioned: a delete is immediate and unrecoverable

egress.terms: Egress and CDN are included in the storage price up to a ratio of 8:1 to total storage; the storage page publishes no price or action above the ratio. GetObject through the single-region S3 gateway usually answers with a redirect to the nearest Hugging Face CDN edge rather than serving the bytes itself.

record.tooling: Any S3 client: AWS CLI, boto3, s5cmd; `hf` CLI (`hf sync`, `hf buckets`); python `huggingface_hub`. For this slot: `git annex initremote type=S3 host=s3.hf.co region=us-east-1 requeststyle=path` (annex needs path-style, which the gateway requires anyway) and `dvc remote add ... ; dvc remote modify myremote endpointurl https://s3.hf.co/<namespace>`. S3 creds are derived from an HF token via 'Generate S3 credentials' (HFAK... key).
record.chaining: Buckets are non-versioned, so a versioning layer on top of the S3 gateway keeps history: DVC is documented as a bucket remote through the gateway, and other S3 clients that take a custom endpoint with path-style addressing reach it the same way; storage is deduplicated at chunk level by Xet, and reads go out through the included CDN.

limits.value: private storage 100 GB on a free user or organisation; public storage 'Best-effort' with no published figure
egress included up to 8:1 of total storage

record.limits_note: The S3 gateway is single-region (us-east-1), path-style only and ListObjectsV2 only, and does not parse aws-chunked trailing checksums (request_checksum_calculation and response_checksum_validation set to when_required); ACLs, bucket policies, object tagging, object versioning, lifecycle rules, server-side encryption and bucket notifications are not supported, user metadata is not stored, server-side copy works within one namespace only, and incomplete multipart uploads expire after 7 days; 2 GB multipart parts are recommended. The per-file and file-count figures on the storage-limits page are stated for Git-backed repositories only.

identity_cost.detail: the join form's first step asks an email address and a password and shows no phone field and no card field, and whether a later step asks a phone number is unverified; free-tier accounts exist with no credit card on file, and a card is asked for PRO, Team, paid compute and storage above the free tier

record.reliability_note: Public storage on a free account is 'Best-effort': above the first few gigabytes the page names abuse mitigations without a figure; bucket deletions are immediate and unrecoverable; the S3 gateway is single-region (us-east-1).
